source_evidence.observation: The theorem takes independent, mean-zero, sub-gaussian random variables X₁,…,X_N and a deterministic coefficient vector a = (a₁,…,a_N) ∈ ℝᴺ.

source_evidence.anchor: [E2] Theorem 2.6.3, complete displayed conclusion, visually checked from the rendered page
source_evidence.observation: For every t ≥ 0, the theorem states the two-sided weighted-sum bound ℙ{|∑_{i=1}^N a_iX_i| ≥ t} ≤ 2 exp(−ct²/(K²‖a‖₂²)), where K = max_i ‖X_i‖_{ψ₂}. Absolute-value bars enclose the entire weighted sum, and the factor 2 is outside the exponential.

The exercise asks the reader to deduce Hoeffding’s inequality for bounded random variables, specifically Theorem 2.2.6, from Theorem 2.6.3, and expressly permits replacing the coefficient 2 in the exponent by some absolute constant.
The referenced theorem assumes that X₁,…,X_N are independent random variables and that X_i ∈ [m_i,M_i] for every i.

For every t > 0, the exact referenced conclusion is ℙ{∑_{i=1}^N (X_i−𝔼X_i) ≥ t} ≤ exp(−2t²/∑_{i=1}^N(M_i−m_i)²). This is a one-sided upper-tail bound and has no multiplicative factor outside the exponential.
A sub-gaussian random variable is one satisfying any of the equivalent properties (i)–(iv) of Proposition 2.5.2, and its norm is ‖X‖_{ψ₂} = inf{t > 0 : 𝔼 exp(X²/t²) ≤ 2}.

source_evidence.anchor: [E7] Restated sub-gaussian tail bound (2.14) and the following sentence
source_evidence.observation: The source’s ψ₂ tail convention is ℙ{|X| ≥ t} ≤ 2 exp(−ct²/‖X‖²_{ψ₂}) for all t ≥ 0, and the source states that c > 0 is an absolute constant.
Every bounded random variable is sub-gaussian and satisfies ‖X‖_{ψ₂} ≤ C‖X‖∞, with the displayed choice C = 1/√(ln 2).

source_evidence.anchor: [E9] Sentence immediately preceding Theorem 2.6.3 and the theorem’s coefficient term
source_evidence.observation: The weighted theorem is obtained by considering a_iX_i, and its denominator uses K²‖a‖₂², with K the maximum individual ψ₂ norm and ‖a‖₂² = ∑_{i=1}^N a_i².

source_evidence.location: PDF pages 6, 16, and 18; printed pages 17, 27, and 29
source_evidence.anchor: [E10] Analyst inference from Theorem 2.2.6, equation (2.17), and Theorem 2.6.3
source_evidence.observation: For nonzero widths d_i := M_i−m_i, set Y_i := (X_i−𝔼X_i)/d_i and a_i := d_i. Then ∑a_iY_i = ∑(X_i−𝔼X_i), while |Y_i| ≤ 1 and equation (2.17) gives a uniform absolute ψ₂ bound. Theorem 2.6.3 consequently gives a two-sided estimate ℙ{|∑(X_i−𝔼X_i)| ≥ t} ≤ 2 exp(−c′t²/∑d_i²), and event inclusion gives the same right-hand side for the one-sided event in Theorem 2.2.6.

contract_plain_english: [E3–E5] For independent bounded random variables X_i ∈ [m_i,M_i], Exercise 2.6.4 asks for the one-sided upper-tail estimate for the centered sum ∑(X_i−𝔼X_i). The exact referenced Theorem 2.2.6 says that, for every t > 0, this probability is at most exp(−2t²/∑(M_i−m_i)²), with no prefactor. The exercise permits replacing the exponent coefficient 2 by a universal positive constant. [E1,E2,E8,E10] The intended deduction normalizes each centered variable by its interval width, uses boundedness to obtain a uniform ψ₂ norm, and applies Theorem 2.6.3 with the widths as coefficients. Theorem 2.6.3 is two-sided: it bounds ℙ{|∑a_iX_i| ≥ t}, with absolute-value bars around the entire sum, by 2 exp(−ct²/(K²‖a‖₂²)). Its specialization therefore gives a two-sided bound 2 exp(−c′t²/∑(M_i−m_i)²), which also bounds the requested one-sided event by containment. The external factor 2 remains in this direct deduction; because the exercise explicitly relaxes only the exponent coefficient, whether that prefactor is accepted as part of the requested variant is a genuine source ambiguity and must not be silently erased.
